llm.summary: This skill matches its stated Aiding Shifu login and work-order purpose, but it handles account tokens and personal data in unsafe, under-disclosed ways that need review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the Aiding Shifu API are purpose-aligned, but sending login QR payloads to api.qrserver.com and invoking local file open commands through child_process expand the environment impact beyond what is clearly documented.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install script or dependency install hook was found, but the distributed package includes a real-looking config.json with a JWT bearer token and personal phone number, which is not appropriate install-time content.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses that tokens are saved to config.json, but it does not clearly disclose third-party QR generation, wildcard postMessage token sharing, token display/copy behavior, console token output, or the breadth of Write/Edit/Execute authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists bearer tokens in plaintext files and browser localStorage without permission hardening, retention controls, or a secure credential store, and it can pass tokens to any opener window using target origin '*'.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The platform-login, technician-search, and work-order capabilities are coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifact also ships a plaintext config containing a bearer token and phone number and exposes newly obtained tokens through UI, logs, local storage, and cross-window messaging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Do not install this version unless you are prepared to review and contain credential exposure. The publisher should remove the packaged config.json secret, revoke the exposed token, stop sending login payloads to third-party QR services, avoid logging or displaying raw tokens, replace wildcard postMessage token transfer, and store credentials in a protected secret store with clear user consent.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Login support is part of the skill purpose, but the verified artifacts show under-disclosed token exposure, third-party QR handling, and local exec usage that are broader than necessary.
[AE1] expected: The referenced sms-login.html and qr-login.html files were present and fully inspected locally, so the coverage concern was not treated as an evasion finding.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: tokens are displayed, copied, stored in localStorage/plaintext config, sent to window.opener with '*', and a packaged config contains a bearer token and phone number.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: run-login.js prints the returned token or identifier to stdout, and login.js prints a token prefix, which is unsafe for authentication material.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: third-party QR generation receives login payloads, and child_process exec is used to open local files; both are avoidable for this workflow.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted: login QR URLs are transmitted to api.qrserver.com, an unrelated QR-generation service, without clear user disclosure.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad login trigger is not by itself a security violation because login is a stated feature and still requires user action, but narrower activation would reduce accidental credential handling.
[P2] expected: The cited material was a normal HTML comment labeling the login form; I did not find artifact-backed hidden agent instructions.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only UI text is consistent with a China-specific Chinese-language business platform and was not treated as a material security concern.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the static scan findings are supported by artifact evidence for bundled credentials, plaintext token persistence, wildcard token messaging, URL query parameters for phone/OTP, and token logging.
